security_spec.violation_condition: In XiangShan RTL, if the final load/store access of a multi-memory-access instruction (Zcmp push/pop, vector load/store) has its dretire signal asserted AFTER the instruction's iretire is asserted (i.e., the data trace retirement pulse occurs in a cycle subsequent to instruction trace retirement), the hardware violates the tightened normative requirement that the final data access 'must be reported no later than when the instruction is reported as retired.' This can occur when the load/store unit's completion pipeline is decoupled from the commit/retirement stage in an out-of-order design, such that a straggling final MMA access completes post-retirement.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: when (dretire && dtype_is_mma && is_final_access_of_instruction && iretire_past) in trace interface output logic; or $past(iretire) && dretire && is_final_mma_access without corresponding iretire in same cycle
security_spec.summary: Spec tightens final MMA data-access retirement deadline from permissive 'may' to normative 'must report no later than instruction retirement,' requiring XiangShan trace-interface RTL to guarantee dretire timing for the last access of Zcmp/vector multi-access instructions does not lag behind iretire.

findings.finding: TracePipe defines only itype, iretire, ilastsize — no dretire field exists. The trace architecture is instruction-retirement-only with no data trace (dretire) support. Since the violation condition requires a dretire signal that does not exist, the described vulnerability cannot manifest in this RTL.

The TraceCoreInterface output to the external encoder carries per-group {itype, iretire, ilastsize, iaddr} only. No dretire or dtype field exists at the core-to-encoder boundary. Data trace retirement is not implemented.

Trace context signals are driven simultaneously with traceValids gated on io.commits.isCommit && io.commits.commitValid(i). Since dretire is not implemented, the iretire-only trace output is internally consistent. There is no scenario where dretire could lag behind iretire because dretire does not exist.
findings.snippet:
for (i <- 0 until CommitWidth) {
  traceBlockInPipe(i).itype := rawInfo(i).traceBlockInPipe.itype
  traceBlockInPipe(i).iretire := iretireCommit(i)
  traceBlockInPipe(i).ilastsize := rawInfo(i).traceBlockInPipe.ilastsize
  traceValids(i) := io.commits.isCommit && io.commits.commitValid(i)

findings.finding: The ROB state machine has only s_idle and s_walk states. There is no s_dretire state because data-only retirement is not implemented. Within the current one-dimensional iretire architecture, this is correct.
findings.snippet:
io.commits.isWalk := state === s_walk
io.commits.isCommit := state === s_idle && !blockCommit

findings.finding: TraceBuffer compresses adjacent trace blocks by accumulating iretire counts. No dretire handling exists, but this is consistent with the one-dimensional iretire-only architecture. The buffer correctly handles the signals it was designed for.
findings.snippet:
blocksUpdate(i).bits.tracePipe.iretire := blocksUpdate(i - 1).bits.tracePipe.iretire + io.in.fromRob.blocks(i).bits.tracePipe.iretire
// No dretire accumulation — dretire not implemented

findings.finding: Rename generates itype for trace. For vector load/store instructions, Itype.jumpTypeGen returns 0.U (None) since they are not branch/jump/xret. No Zcmp-specific itype generation exists because Zcmp instructions (cm.push/cm.pop) are not implemented in XiangShan. No MMA classification for trace purposes.
findings.snippet:
uops(i).traceBlockInPipe.itype := Mux(
  isXret, Itype.ExpIntReturn,
  Itype.jumpTypeGen(inVec(i).fuType, inVec(i).fuOpType, ...)
)

findings.finding: CtrlBlock passes trace output as a pure identity mapping for iretire/itype/ilastsize. No dretire path exists, which is consistent with the not-implemented state of data trace retirement.

The only dynamic trace update in the ROB is branch-taken feedback (NonTaken->Taken). No post-commit data-side trace update mechanism exists, confirming that once an instruction retires, its trace data is final. With no dretire feature, this is correct.
MemBlock trace bypass passes iretire/itype/ilastsize/iaddr through register stages to L2Top. No dretire or dtype fields exist in this path. Consistent with the not-implemented data trace feature.

TraceBlock contains iaddr/ftqIdx, ftqOffset, and tracePipe (itype, iretire, ilastsize). No dretire or dtype field. This is the fundamental storage unit in all trace pipeline stages. Without a dretire field, the described vulnerability (dretire after iretire for final MMA access) cannot occur.

Dispatch's isPush/isPop extraction uses Itype.isPush/isPop which only maps to standard jal/jalr RAS patterns for front-end prediction, not Zcmp multi-register stack operations. Zcmp (cm.push/cm.pop/cm.popret/cm.popretz) instructions are not decoded, dispatched, or executed anywhere in the current RTL.
